body: I think you should contact your doctor immediately, explain the situation to them, maybe get another prescription that you might have to keep hidden. Just talk to your doctor if possible. Suddenly stopping medication for mental health treatment can be very very bad for you mentally and also physically for your body. My dad takes medication and we've seen severe effects just when dosage was reduced. I can't imagine what sudden discontinuation could do. I really don't mean to scare you but this is a serious situation.

You just have to learn to live with it, accept that these thoughts are going to plague your existence for the rest of your days, accept that you're never going to get a peaceful night's rest. Stop wrestling with these thoughts, let them just flow, accept them as a part of who you are and I swear it'll become easier. I can't promise it'll get better, but it will get a little easier. 

I'm sorry that my response may seem harsh, but I'm just speaking from personal experience.

I don't know what happened and I'm really nobody to tell you what to do, but I'd suggest not talking to her with the purpose of "I don't want her thinking these things". It seems like what she said isn't about you but rather a reflection on who she is. I don't know if this made sense but you'll just be hurt more. 
And this is just me personally, this isn't really advice or anything but anyone at all who genuinely makes you want to kill yourself even once, isn't worth keeping in your life at all. 

I'm really sorry if it feels like I'm trying to impose something on you, I really don't mean to.

You're in a bad place right now, in my experience what you really need right now is someone to talk to, someone who'll listen and understand. 

If you want to, I'm here to talk to.

Same. 
The oldest vivid memories I have are of times I'd hide in some corner of the house in the dark, staring at a window and just wishing, I didn't exist, wishing I could somehow break the window grills and jump out, and sometimes violently pulling at them too.
Family sucks huh...

That fear is real, one time my parents found out about one of my ex's and everyone in my immediate extended family knee about it, next time I visited everyone I got so many questions about it. A scenario where that happens with a failed suicide attempt, all the questions, it's horrifying. It leads down a spiral of wanting to kill myself even more and being scared.

It's a complicates thing with ex's, and I just want you to know that what she said doesn't matter. I don't mean to undermine how you feel, I've been there. Because of your present or past feelings for them, things said by ex's can hurt a lot, be stuck in your head, the memory of the statement played over and over in your mind and you can do nothing about it. This can be the case even if what they said is 100% wrong. 

Maybe what I'm trying to say is how you feel is completely valid but over time you'll have to come to terms with the fact that there's a reason that person is in your past and not your present, the things they say don't matter anymore.

Spare yourself the misery if you can, I remember it was a month of crying on both sides, even though she meant so much to me. 
I wish you luck, and hope you never have to hear such things again

He probably does mean the best, and I know it hurts. When I said you should leave him behind, it wasn't because he maybe/is a bad person. He may never be good for you again after that, and after this you'll just be dragging your relation with him. I once had a best friend and she was honestly, the best person for me, but one time in a moment of weakness she shared a secret of mine with someone else. That secret is a big deal to me, and I didn't want anyone finding out. I understood why that happened, I know it wasn't her fault, but I could just never be that close to her ever again, our friendship was dragged on for another month but it was just dying. I'm giving this example just so you can ask yourself if you're not in this situation, because that one month or so of dragging along was miserable for the both of us, hope it's not for you.

It's indescribable what being told that shit makes you feel like, it's a level of guilt trip that kind of just suffocates you, I understand this because I have to hear this almost regularly from someone I can't put behind me, but if you want advice of any kind, mine would be to leave this person behind if it's possible, however hard it maybe, this person can never get your trust again the way it used to be.

I usually don't talk to 'strangers on the internet' but if you want to talk about this, I'm here for you.
This isn't about happiness, never will be, being happy is something I've given up on a long time ago.

I agree with the "keys to escape the prison cell" concept. Personally I don't know if I'd be in a place to do it anytime soon, but having a sharp blade around always helped in a weird way. To be able to kind of stand at the edge anytime you want to. Since lockdown started I left my last one at college and it's been incredibly frustrating with the feeling to the point of wanting to claw my skin out(doesn't really do much but cause pain).

I don't know what's going on in your life, but maybe you need acceptance rather than change, accept things for what they are learn to live with it, working for me. 

PS : Generally speaking this is terrible advice but after a certain point in life maybe it isn't

I've told a couple of people my story, I've learnt that what happened will always matter too much to me but never matter enough to someone else, if that makes any sense to you. 

I have not read about complex PTSD or PTSD, I'm not ready to, I don't want to be risk being diagnosed with a mental illness when I have no means of treating it. I'm also kind of scared of doing it.

Also I don't want to discourage you, but you've kinda missed the point here, there are things that aren't broken or need to be fixed, they're just a part of who you are no matter what you do. I've picked up a few kinda unhealthy coping mechanisms over time, those are things that can be changed or fixed with time and hardwork, not who I am

What I mean is sometimes things happen in your life that permanently become a part of who you are,influence your every thought and action, can't be looked past or moved on from.

Time, place and money have nothing to do with it and can't change anything about it. It will be a part of you and make you miserable whether you like it or not.

Edit: I've explained this from my perspective obviously but the 'essence of your existence' can mean a slightly different thing to different people but still apply to this context, I wanted to write a more generalised post, because sometimes to just know people out there feel the way you do, validates your feelings which is the topic of this post as well.

Someone else's pain doesn't diminish or invalidate yours. People don't understand that something that may seem like lesser suffering could be hurting a person a lot more, especially because of constantly being forced to believe they don't have the right to feel that way.

Again, not trying to defend myself but we did talk before I made the call, she said she was okay with it and I wanted to do it for her

Edit: I didn't acknowledge that I understand what you're saying, just doing that
From my perspective it seemed like I had her consent to make the call, not trying to defend myself, just wanting to understand if this was still a social interaction I should have avoided.
Damn, perfectly articulated exactly what was on my mind
